title: USB Type-C receptacle, USB 2.0 device (sink) port, 16 or 24 contact
sources: USB Type-C Cable and Connector Specification, Release 1.0, chapter 4, Table 4-14 (Rd 5.1 kOhm), as cited in interfaces.md [S2]
GCT USB4105 drawing rev B4, pinout and shell, as cited in interfaces.md [S1]

rules.text: All VBUS pads share one net.
All GND pads share one net.
The GND pads are on the board's ground net.
VBUS is not ground: a swapped power pair.
VBUS and GND are different nets.
CC1 and CC2 are separate nets: one resistor each, not one shared.
CC1 and CC2 each carry a 5.1 kOhm +/-10 % pulldown to GND (4.59 to 5.61 kOhm).
A device port shows no pullup from CC to VBUS.
On a 16-pin part Dp1 joins Dp2 and Dn1 joins Dn2.
D+ and D- are different nets.
Every shield pad is tied to GND or a stated chassis network (X-SHD-01).
A TVS or ESD array covers VBUS, D+ and D-, CC1 and CC2, or the exemption is recorded in PARTS[ref].ifcheck_exempt (X-ESD-01).

notes: UC-ALL-02's 5 mm stub length and UC-ALL-04's 5 mm TVS distance (X-ESD-02) are placement checks this definition does not make.
UC-ALL-06 (the case opening admits the 12.35 x 6.50 mm overmold plus 0.5 mm per side) is a case check: case_verify.py connector_openings with margin=0.5 and a mating_body sized to the overmold.
A USB-C receptacle that belongs to a module (a nice!nano) declares PARTS[ref].interface_wiring = "module": the netlist rules are reported SKIP and only the mating rules run.
